newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia Group to restructure business in rescue bid.
newsitem.headline: Kia Group to restructure business in rescue bid.

text.p: South Korea's troubled Kia Group will cut the number of its domestic affiliates to 13 by merging and selling units, and raise 3.1 trillion won by selling real estate in a rescue attempt, the Korea First Bank said on Tuesday.
The nation's eighth largest conglomerate has submitted its self-rescue package to its creditor banks, a Korea First spokesman said.

The spokesman at Korea First, Kia's major creditor, said Kia also planned to save 491.2 billion won by freezing wage increases and curtailing its executives above the director level by 30 percent and middle management by 18 percent.
Another 565.3 billion won was planned to be saved by cutting production costs and overhead expenditures.
The spokesman said Kia would slim down by reducing the number of domestic affiliates to 13 from the current 28. Kia has 10 affiliates abroad at present.
Construction affiliate Kisan Co would be spun off from Kia Group but no details were given.
